item.title: What to Know About Bank Melli, Singled Out in U.S. Call for Economic War
item.description: Bank Melli, Iran’s largest lender, already faces waves of sanctions that severely limit its ability to operate abroad. Every foreign branch must be shut down, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
item.dc:creator: Lara Jakes and James Paton
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: The main branch of Bank Melli in Tehran last year.

item.title: Worker Dies After Accident With Plane at Montreal Airport
item.description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada said the episode involved an Airbus A350 operated by French Bee, a French low-cost airline.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:description: The authority that operates Montréal-Trudeau International Airport said a worker employed by Samsic, a company that provides support services, was killed in an accident on Monday.

item.title: Dozens Massacred in Haiti, Officials Say, Heightening Fears of Gangs
item.description: Gangs targeted a key community on the outskirts of the capital, raising fears about the gangs’ next move. The mayor said at least 25 people had been killed, but the U.N. put the death toll at 47.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles and André Paultre
item.media:description: Dozens of people were killed by armed gangs in Kenscoff, a neighborhood near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on Sunday into Monday, officials said.

item.title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The U.S. Steel Clairton Coke Plant in Clairton, Pa. Canada has announced it will impose retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American products including steel.

item.title: Christian Convert Who Fled Iran and Was Deported By Trump Finds New Home
item.description: Artemis Ghasemzadeh, who had escaped religious persecution, was deported to Panama under Trump’s immigration crackdown. Now, Canada has given her asylum.
item.dc:creator: Farnaz Fassihi
item.media:credit: Alana Paterson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Artemis Ghasemzadeh at her new home on Denman Island near Vancouver.

item.title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
item.description: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff and Ana Swanson
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada speaking about the trade dispute with the United States on Monday at the Davie Shipyard in Levis, Quebec.

item.title: U.S. Tariffs Could Price Canadian Firms Out of U.S. and Threaten Thousands of Jobs
item.description: The 50 percent tariffs President Trump imposed on Canadian exports to the United States will make it impossible for many Canadian companies to continue to sell to the U.S. market, economists say.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Harvested logs in British Columbia in 2023. Canada’s forestry industry may be hit particularly hard by the latest American tariffs.

item.title: Trump Threatens New 50% Tariffs on Cars, Trucks and Steel as U.S.-Canada Trade War Unfolds
item.description: President Trump vowed to increase tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and steel to 50 percent starting Jan. 1, as the countries edged toward a full-blown trade war.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Tony Romm
item.media:description: Trade tensions between the United States and Canada have spiraled over the past few days, after the two sides failed to reach a trade deal and President Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion of the country’s exports on Saturday.

item.title: Can ‘Argentina’s Texas’ Save the Country’s Economy?
item.description: Thousands of Argentines are flocking to a remote stretch of Patagonia, seeking work with only backpacks, tents and the hope that they and their country can turn around their fortunes.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola and Sarah Pabst

item.title: How Argentina’s Oil Boom Is Changing Patagonia
item.description: Our correspondent Emma Bubola travels to northwest Patagonia, the epicenter of an oil boom that Argentina hopes will revolutionize its economy.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola, Leila Medina, Rebecca Suner, Sarah Pabst and Joey Sendaydiego

item.title: U.S.-Canada Trade War: What to Know About Tariffs and the Negotiations
item.description: Canada suspended trade negotiations, triggering President Trump’s 50 percent tariffs on a range of Canadian goods. Mark Carney retaliated “dollar for dollar.”
item.dc:creator: The New York Times
item.media:description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addresses the trade dispute with the United States in Levis, Quebec, on Aug. 24.

item.title: What Canadian Goods Will Take Trump’s 50% Tariffs? Some Pretty Strange Items.
item.description: Buoys, dog muzzles, capes, national flags and “base metal statuettes” from Canada are now more expensive for U.S. shoppers.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen

item.title: Echoing Trump, Latin America’s Leaders Boost Allies Across Borders
item.description: With cheers, endorsements and insults for rivals and “wokismo,” a new crop of right-wing leaders are openly stepping into one another’s elections.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola, Annie Correal and Ana Ionova
item.media:description: President Javier Milei of Argentina, left, with Flávio Bolsonaro, who hopes to be Brazil’s next president, last month. Mr. Milei’s strident support of Mr. Bolsonaro’s candidacy led to a rift with the current Brazilian president.

item.title: Mexican Governor Accused by U.S. of Aiding Cartel Leaves Office, Again
item.description: Rubén Rocha Moya of Sinaloa reversed course a day after returning to office, amid widespread criticism, including from members of his own party.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner and Lars Dolder
item.media:description: Rubén Rocha Moya in 2024.

item.title: Carney Slams U.S.-Canada Trade Proposal and Vows Retaliation
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney gave a powerful speech to Canadians on Saturday morning, hours after ordering negotiators to suspend U.S. trade talks despite President Trump’s punishing tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:credit: Patrick Doyle/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said that he had pulled negotiators out of trade talks with the United States because the Trump administration had “asked too much and offered too little.”

item.title: Waking Up to an Escalating Canada-U.S. Trade War
item.description: The two countries are locked in a potentially devastating tariff war after last-minute demands ended talks in Washington late Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:description: Dominic LeBlanc and Janice Charette at the Canadian Embassy in Washington in June.

item.title: Carney Stands Up to Trump in U.S.-Canada Trade War
item.description: Canada’s prime minister walked away from what he thought was a bad trade deal with the United States. Many Canadians are behind him, but it will be costly.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:credit: Patrick Doyle/The Canadian Press, Associated Press
item.media:description: Mark Carney, Canada’s prime minister, said on Saturday that “Canada is becoming stronger and less dependent on America.”

item.title: Canada-U.S. Trade War Escalates as Talks Collapse
item.description: Intense negotiations to stave off new levies by the Trump administration ended in an impasse as Mark Carney suspended talks. U.S. tariffs on Canada, and retaliatory tariffs on the U.S., will come into effect.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff, Ian Austen and Ana Swanson
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said he suspended the trade talks because the American side introduced last-minute terms that ”called into question the reliability of any deal.”

item.title: Mexican Governor, Accused by U.S. of Helping Cartel, Returns to His Job
item.description: After U.S. prosecutors accused Gov. Rubén Rocha Moya of protecting the Sinaloa cartel, he said he would step down to focus on his defense. On Friday, he declared he was back and faced much criticism.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner
item.media:description: Rubén Rocha Moya, the governor of Sinaloa state, during an annual earthquake drill in Culiacán, Mexico, in 2024.

item.title: Canada-U.S. Tariff Talks Continue as Trump’s Midnight Deadline Looms
item.description: Canadian negotiators were in Washington to finalize a deal that would stave off new tariffs and improve the terms of existing ones, but Mark Carney faces a tough sell back home.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: The ArcelorMittal Dofasco steel plant in Hamilton, Ontario. President Trump hit the Canadian steel industry with tariffs of up to 50 percent last year.

item.title: Machel Montano, Soca Sovereign, Takes Over Brooklyn Public Library

item.dc:creator: Patricia Meschino
item.media:description: “Journey of a Soca King” opens Saturday and runs to Sept. 12.

item.title: Rare South American Diseases Offer Clues on the Next Pandemic
item.description: Ebola virus, hantavirus and the pathogen that causes Covid-19 likely jumped from animals to humans. So do these viruses — and scientists say climate change is speeding their spread.
item.dc:creator: Zane Irwin, Lucía Cholakian Herrera and Sebastián López Brach
item.media:credit: Sebastián López Brach for The New York Times

item.description: After a deadline extension, the latest U.S. tariff threats seemed headed toward resolution on Wednesday, but questions lingered about what Canada would give up, and what it would get in exchange.
